monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.placement: Labridae; unique combination of plesiomorphic and derived features (position within the family unresolved)
monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.source: Bannikov A.F. & Carnevale G. (2010) Geodiversitas 32(2): 201-220, 'Measurements (as percentage of SL)': HL 31, maximum body depth 41, snout to first dorsal-fin spine 42. Holotype MCSNV IGVR 71214/71215, 34 mm SL.

monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.placement: oldest substantiated pomacentrid; 'relatively generalized Recent pomacentrid' body form
monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.source: Bellwood D.R. & Sorbini L. (1996) Zool. J. Linn. Soc. 117: 159-174. Holotype MCSNV IG 23692: SL 20.5 mm, maximum body depth 9.0 mm (43.9%); paratype BMNH P.5126: SL 29.5 mm, depth 15.0 mm (50.8%).

monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.placement: Sparidae (Sparnodus); value is the deepest-bodied Sparnodus specimen recorded (holotype of 'Pomadasys' furcatus = S. elongatus), typical individuals are shallower
monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.source: Bannikov A.F. (2006) Geodiversitas 28(2): 249-275: 'SL/maximum body depth ratio is 2.1' for MNHN Bol 68/69, 'equal in depth to the most deep-bodied specimens of Sparnodus ever recorded'.
monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.note: upper bound for the genus; no typical-specimen value is given in the source

monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.placement: Sparidae (new genus for Dentex crassispinus Agassiz)
monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.source: Bannikov A.F. (2006) Geodiversitas 28(2): 249-275: head length contained 3.25 times in SL (30.8%); head length 1.17 times less than body depth (-> 36.0% SL). Holotype MNHN Bol 8/9, 128 mm SL.
Bannikov A.F. (2006) Geodiversitas 28(2): 249-275, diagnosis: 'Head length 3.03 in SL. Maximum body depth 3.26 in SL.' Holotype MNHN Bol 14a/14b, 261 mm SL.

monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.source: Bannikov A.F. (2006) Geodiversitas 28(2): 249-275, Table 3 (lectotype MNHN Bol 275 and paralectotype Bol 24): head length 32 (30), maximum body depth 34 (34), snout to spiny dorsal fin 40 (39) % SL.

monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.placement: stem Siganidae (most basal fossil siganid genus in Tyler & Bannikov 1997)
monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.source: Tyler J.C. & Bannikov A.F. (1997) Smithsonian Contributions to Paleobiology 84: 'the greatest body depth is 41%-43% SL in R. bannikovi versus 23%-34% in R. spinosus'.
Tyler J.C. & Bannikov A.F. (1997) Smithsonian Contributions to Paleobiology 84 (see R. bannikovi).

monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.placement: putative stem Leiognathidae (new subfamily Eoleiognathinae); formerly 'Pygaeus dorsalis'
monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.source: Bannikov A.F. (2014) Studi e Ricerche sui Giacimenti Terziari di Bolca XV: neotype MCSNV T94/T95, 24.5 mm SL, maximum body depth 48% SL.

monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.placement: Ephippidae, closely allied to Platax (Blot 1969; Carnevale et al. 2014)
monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.source: No published ratio located (Blot 1969 monograph not online). Range estimated by the author from two photographed specimens: MCSNV specimen (Wikimedia Commons 'Eoplatax papilio 376.jpg', CC BY-SA 4.0, Ghedoghedo) and NHMW specimen (Wikimedia Commons 'Eoplatax Vienna.jpg', CC BY 2.0), measuring body depth at the dorsal/anal fin bases (excluding the elongate fin webs) over snout-to-hypural length. Blot (1969) describes the body as about as deep as, or deeper than, long.
monte_bolca_published_ratio_test.note: photograph-derived estimate; the discriminating question (deep Platax-like body vs. the 0.57-0.77 stem prediction) is robust to the measurement uncertainty
